speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning. I see you're experiencing fatigue, flank pain, and fever following recent antibiotic treatment for acute sinusitis. To understand what might be happening, have you noticed any changes in your urine, such as color, frequency, or urgency? Also, have you experienced any nausea or vomiting alongside these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has your urine appeared cloudy, bloody, or foul-smelling, and do you have burning during urination? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with culture and sensitivity.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis with culture and sensitivity: Leukocyturia Present, Bacterial Culture Negative, Cytospin Stained With Hansel's Solution shows 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm.

speaker: Doctor
text: That presence of binucleated eosinophilic cells in your urine is a strong indicator of Acute Interstitial Nephritis, likely triggered by an allergic reaction to the antibiotics you recently took. Do you have a history of allergies, particularly to penicillin or sulfonamides? REQUEST IMAGES: Renal ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis (AIN) secondary to antibiotic allergy. The presence of eosinophilic casts (binucleated cells) in your urine, combined with your history of a rash after amoxicillin and symptoms persisting despite switching antibiotics, confirms this allergic reaction affecting your kidneys.
